newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa unveils bid to promote film industry.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa unveils bid to promote film industry.

text.p: South Africa on Thursday unveiled plans to promote a post-apartheid film industry and try to wean movie fans off Hollywood imports.
Lionel Mtshali, arts and culture minister, told a news conference the government had set aside 10 million rand ($2.1 million) for the project.
"A well-developed film industry will enable South African audiences to (make) their own interpretations of their experience and stories reflected on local screens," he said.
The plan was unveiled on the first day of an international film and television market, being held in southern Africa for the first time.

Organisers said executives from 20th Century Fox, Columbia Pictures, Warner Brothers and MGM were among those attending the market, intended to expose regional film-makers and service providers to a wider audience.
Mtshali said his department wanted among other things to "develop audiences receptive to local-content films" and to train local script-writers and producers.

He said a film and television foundation would be set up to oversee the process. It would study financial incentives to encourage private enterprise to invest in film and video projects, Mtshali said.
